newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kesko, Sentra jump on Tuko deal.
newsitem.headline: Kesko, Sentra jump on Tuko deal.

text.p: Shares in Finnish wholesale and retail groups Kesko Oy and Sentra Oy rose sharply on Monday following Kesko's announcement last Friday, that it would sell its Tuko unit to various buyers, including Sentra, brokers said.
At 1125/0925 GMT, Kesko traded at 71.50 markka, up 5.00 markka or more than seven percent. Trade was a lively 21 million markka.
OTC-listed Sentra's more liquied A share traded at 260.00 markka, up 100.00 markka or more than 60 percent. Trade was 1.6 million markka, which is active for the stock.

"There had been fears that Kesko would make a loss on the Tuko deal, but now those fears seem to have been unfounded," one broker said, adding that investors now expected the European Commission to approve the sale of Tuko's parts and this reflected on Kesko's share price.

Kesko last May said it planned to merge with its rival Tuko, but the European Commission blocked the transaction in November on the basis that it would damage competition on the Finnish daily goods market.
Brokers said Sentra shares gained on improved earnings potential after it acquired Tuko's Suomen Spar retail operations from Kesko.
